question.prompt: A backordered request for 12 repair parts is split across two vendors: 7 and 5 units. The original delivery promise and request ID remain the customer’s reference until all parts arrive. Which model transition preserves the invariant?

options.text: Keep the original request ID and promise; allocate all 12 units across both vendors, and leave it open until both arrive.
Close the original request and create unrelated requests for 7 and 5 units with new customer promises.
Mark the original fulfilled when the first vendor ships, then treat the second shipment as a new request.

feedback.reason: The split is valid only if the child allocations account for all 12 units while the original request identity and promise remain active until fulfillment completes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The split preserves one parent obligation only if child quantities conserve the requested total and the parent remains open through fulfillment.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is split allocations remain under original promise and total 12; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Replacing the request identity breaks the retained customer promise and loses lineage. First-shipment completion cannot satisfy the full quantity obligation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the customer explicitly cancels or revises the promise, that is a separate transition with recorded authorization.
details.transfer: For decomposition, preserve the parent obligation and make the conservation condition explicit across its parts.

messages.text: Replacing the request identity breaks the retained customer promise and loses lineage.
First-shipment completion cannot satisfy the full quantity obligation.

question.prompt: A garden plot is reserved by Ada. A transfer to Bo must preserve the plot boundary and approval history, and Bo must accept before Ada’s reservation ends. What is the legal transition?

options.text: End Ada’s reservation first, then create a new unrelated reservation for Bo and copy the history later.
Record one transfer that links the same plot and history to Bo, and commit it only when Bo accepts.
Change the plot boundary to fit Bo’s request and mark the transfer accepted before Bo responds.

feedback.reason: A transfer must preserve the same plot and history and cannot leave ownership unassigned between Ada and Bo; acceptance is the stated precondition.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Transfer continuity keeps the same plot and history, while recipient acceptance is a prerequisite to changing its reservation holder.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is same plot/history persist; recipient acceptance precedes transfer; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Ending and recreating loses continuity and creates a gap in the recorded reservation history. Changing the plot violates the invariant, and acceptance has not yet occurred.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If Bo declines, retain Ada’s active reservation; a boundary change needs a distinct reviewed operation.
details.transfer: When ownership moves between parties, preserve the governed resource and commit only after the receiving party meets the acceptance condition.

messages.text: Ending and recreating loses continuity and creates a gap in the recorded reservation history.
Changing the plot violates the invariant, and acceptance has not yet occurred.

question.prompt: A regional subscription bundle contains components priced at 30 and 20 units with a declared discount of 5. Draft bundles may be edited, but published price must equal component total minus that discount. Which publication transition is legal?

options.text: Publish the draft’s entered price even if it is 40 because the catalog manager supplied it.
Publish at 50 and apply the 5-unit discount later during checkout.
Publish only at 45, recomputed from the committed component prices and discount.

feedback.reason: The invariant is checked at publication: 30 + 20 − 5 = 45, so a different stored price cannot enter the published state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Publication recomputes price from the exact committed components and discount; a mismatched total cannot enter published state.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is published price equals 30+20-5 using the same values committed; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: A manually entered value of 40 contradicts the stated pricing rule. Deferring the discount creates a published representation whose price is inconsistent with its components.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The draft can remain editable; once published, changing components or discount requires a new validated publication.
details.transfer: Evaluate derived totals from the exact component and policy values being committed, then transition only if the invariant holds.

messages.text: A manually entered value of 40 contradicts the stated pricing rule.
Deferring the discount creates a published representation whose price is inconsistent with its components.

question.prompt: A charging station has two compatible sockets. A reservation is held for five minutes and expires if not confirmed. Both sockets are currently held, and one hold has expired before a new request arrives. Which state update is valid?

options.text: Release the expired hold, then admit the new one only if capacity remains at commit.
Count the expired hold as active until an operator clears it, so no request can proceed.
Confirm both the expired reservation and new request because they were each valid when first submitted.

feedback.reason: Capacity is based on active holds; the expired reservation no longer consumes a socket, while the new request still needs a valid capacity check when recorded.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Expiry releases a held socket; capacity admission checks only active reservations at the commit point.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is expired hold releases socket; active reservations remain <=2; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Treating an expired hold as active leaves the model in a state that contradicts its expiry rule. The old request’s earlier validity does not keep it confirmed after its hold expires.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If capacity is full after rechecking, reject or waitlist according to policy; do not exceed two active reservations.
details.transfer: For expiring reservations, make expiry and capacity release part of the state model, then validate capacity at the transition that admits a new hold.

messages.text: Treating an expired hold as active leaves the model in a state that contradicts its expiry rule.
The old request’s earlier validity does not keep it confirmed after its hold expires.

question.prompt: An archive asset keeps a permanent asset ID. Two catalog entries are discovered to describe the same asset, but each has different source provenance; descriptive tags can be merged only with curator review. Which merge transition is legal?

options.text: Delete one asset and discard its provenance because the tags are being combined.
Keep the asset ID and both provenance records; apply only curator-approved tag changes.
Replace the permanent asset ID with the merged tag set and mark the merge complete automatically.

feedback.reason: Identity and provenance are not descriptive tags; a reviewed merge can reconcile metadata while retaining the asset’s lineage.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The merge changes curator-approved descriptions but preserves permanent asset identity and source provenance.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is permanent ID and both provenance records retained; tag merge requires review; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Discarding provenance violates the explicit source-history requirement. Tags are mutable descriptions, not a valid replacement for the permanent identity or approval.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A curator may reject a proposed tag conflict without merging the underlying source records.
details.transfer: When merging descriptive data, preserve identity and provenance separately from values that curators may reconcile.

messages.text: Discarding provenance violates the explicit source-history requirement.
Tags are mutable descriptions, not a valid replacement for the permanent identity or approval.

question.prompt: A usage approval is drafted for one territory and expires at 18:00 on a stated date. Activation requires both fields to be explicit and the expiry to be in the future at activation. Which transition should the model allow?

options.text: Activate the draft with a blank territory and infer the territory from the user’s account later.
Activate an expired approval because it was valid when the draft was created.
Activate only with an explicit territory and expiry still in the future.

feedback.reason: Activation depends on the complete scope and on expiry still being future at the transition; the draft alone does not satisfy those conditions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Activation checks explicit territory and future expiry at the transition that makes the approval effective.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is territory explicit and expiry future at activation; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Account inference supplies a different scope than the explicit-approval invariant requires. Validity when drafted does not establish validity at a later activation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A correction to territory or expiry creates a revised draft that must pass activation validation again.
details.transfer: Check time-sensitive prerequisites at the state transition that makes the approval effective, using explicit scope values.

messages.text: Account inference supplies a different scope than the explicit-approval invariant requires.
Validity when drafted does not establish validity at a later activation.

question.prompt: A battery can be assigned to only one aircraft at a time. A replacement moves it from Aircraft A to Aircraft B, and the maintenance record must show both the old and new assignments. What is a legal transition?

options.text: Move assignment from A to B atomically; retain both history records.
Open B’s assignment first and leave A active until a later cleanup job runs.
Delete A’s assignment and create B’s without retaining the prior maintenance history.

feedback.reason: The invariant forbids two simultaneous active assignments; one atomic move can preserve the history and prevent an invalid intermediate state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Exclusive assignment requires moving from old to new as one transition while retaining both assignment records.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is single active aircraft; old/new assignment history retained; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: The overlap temporarily violates the one-aircraft rule and can be observed before cleanup. Deleting the old record loses the required assignment history.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If B is not eligible, leave A’s assignment active and reject the move.
details.transfer: For exclusive assignment, treat reassignment as one transition over the old and new relationships, preserving history without exposing dual ownership.

messages.text: The overlap temporarily violates the one-aircraft rule and can be observed before cleanup.
Deleting the old record loses the required assignment history.

question.prompt: A referral is queued for a specialist, but patient consent is revoked before the outbound disclosure is sent. The transition to disclosed state requires active consent at send time. What should happen?

options.text: Send the referral because consent was active when the referral was queued.
Keep it undisclosed after consent is revoked; record the blocked transition.
Mark it disclosed and remove the consent history after the send attempt.

feedback.reason: The disclosure transition is conditional on consent at sending; revocation removes that prerequisite before the external effect occurs.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Consent must remain active at disclosure time; queue-time authorization alone cannot authorize the external send.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is consent revoked before send; no disclosure transition; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Queue time does not satisfy the explicit send-time consent rule. Marking it disclosed would state an external disclosure that was not authorized or performed.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The navigator may obtain renewed consent and submit a new authorized disclosure attempt.
details.transfer: Revalidate changing authorization at the transition that crosses the protected boundary, and retain the reason that blocked it.

messages.text: Queue time does not satisfy the explicit send-time consent rule.
Marking it disclosed would state an external disclosure that was not authorized or performed.

question.prompt: An exercise attempt pins revision 8 and scoring policy 3 at its start. A learner submits after the deadline, and the policy says late attempts remain incomplete rather than receiving a score. Which state transition is valid?

options.text: Complete it under revision 9 and the current scoring policy because those are now published.
Complete it under revision 8 but silently ignore the deadline.
Keep it incomplete; record no score after the deadline.

feedback.reason: The attempt’s pinned revision and policy do not override the explicit late rule; late submission is not a completed scored attempt.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The attempt’s pinned revision and policy remain its context, but late submission still fails the completion precondition.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is late attempts remain incomplete under pinned attempt context; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Changing pinned versions would make the attempt inconsistent with its start record. Ignoring the deadline violates the completion condition.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separate late-review process could be modeled if the product later defines one; it is not implied here.
details.transfer: A state transition should use the attempt’s pinned context and enforce the condition that determines whether completion is legal.

messages.text: Changing pinned versions would make the attempt inconsistent with its start record.
Ignoring the deadline violates the completion condition.

question.prompt: An exception request can be approved only by the designated approver, below a fixed ceiling, after required controls pass. The approver is authorized, but the control record is missing. Which transition is legal?

options.text: Keep the request pending-controls and record no approval until required controls pass.
Approve it because the approver is authorized and run controls after funds are released.
Move it to rejected permanently even though the missing control may later be supplied.

feedback.reason: Approver authority is necessary but not sufficient; the transition remains pending while a required control is absent.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Approver authority does not replace the missing required control; pending-controls is temporary, not terminal rejection.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is designated approver exists but required control record is missing; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Releasing before controls pass bypasses the stated control order. A missing prerequisite is not evidence that the exception is permanently invalid.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Once the control result arrives, the approver can decide against the same bounded request.
details.transfer: Distinguish a temporarily unsatisfied precondition from a terminal rejection, and do not commit the consequential transition early.

messages.text: Releasing before controls pass bypasses the stated control order.
A missing prerequisite is not evidence that the exception is permanently invalid.

question.prompt: A recording replacement maps annotations by stable segment IDs. One old segment has no match in the proposed revision, and no annotation may be orphaned. Which replacement transition preserves the invariant?

options.text: Replace the revision and attach the unmatched annotation to the segment with the closest timestamp.
Keep the old revision active until every annotation has a reviewed target.
Activate the new revision and leave the orphaned annotation hidden until someone notices it.

feedback.reason: The transition is not legal while an annotation lacks its required stable target; rejection keeps the old valid revision intact.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Every annotation must retain a stable target before the replacement revision becomes active.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is all annotations retain stable targets before revision activation; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Timestamp proximity is not the stable-ID mapping rule and can attach annotation to the wrong segment. A hidden orphan still violates the no-orphan invariant.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A curator can supply a reviewed mapping or retire the annotation through an explicit operation before retry.
details.transfer: Before replacing a referenced structure, validate every dependent reference and keep the last valid state if one cannot be mapped.

messages.text: Timestamp proximity is not the stable-ID mapping rule and can attach annotation to the wrong segment.
A hidden orphan still violates the no-orphan invariant.

question.prompt: A role grant becomes active after approval and expires at a fixed time. At expiry it must no longer authorize requests. A later extension requires a new approval record. Which transition is valid at expiry?

options.text: Keep it active until a user next opens the permissions screen.
Move it back to active automatically when its recipient makes a request.
Expire the grant; require a separately approved grant for extension.

feedback.reason: Expiry changes the grant’s legal state independent of whether a screen is opened; extension is a distinct approval-backed decision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Expiry changes the grant’s legal state without UI activity; a later extension is a new approval-backed grant.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is at expiry grant no longer authorizes; extension needs new approval; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: A user interface visit cannot be the condition for enforcing a stated expiry. A request is not the required new approval and cannot reactivate the expired grant.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A new grant may refer to the prior grant for history while having its own approval and expiry.
details.transfer: Model expiry as a legal transition, not a display update, and treat renewed authority as a new authorized change.

messages.text: A user interface visit cannot be the condition for enforcing a stated expiry.
A request is not the required new approval and cannot reactivate the expired grant.

question.prompt: A notary seals an immutable document revision only after the signer confirms the exact revision digest. The signer rejects the request. Which state transition is legal?

options.text: Keep the revision unsealed and record the rejected digest.
Mark the revision sealed because the request was sent to the signer.
Change the digest to the latest document revision and mark the old request accepted.

feedback.reason: A rejected signer response means the sealing precondition did not complete; the revision must not enter sealed state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The sealed state requires signer confirmation bound to the exact immutable revision digest.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is signer rejection means no seal; target digest remains exact; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Sending a request does not establish signer confirmation. Changing the target revision cannot convert a rejection into confirmation of a different digest.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A corrected revision requires its own signing attempt and confirmation.
details.transfer: Make a terminal state depend on the specific required acknowledgement and bind that acknowledgement to the exact version it authorizes.

messages.text: Sending a request does not establish signer confirmation.
Changing the target revision cannot convert a rejection into confirmation of a different digest.

question.prompt: A payout can be released only for a settled order and once per payout ID. The order is settled and the payout is already marked released with a ledger reference. What should a repeated release command do to domain state?

options.text: Transition released back to proposed and create a replacement ledger entry.
Keep released state and ledger reference; create no second effect.
Create a second release with the same ID, then reconcile duplicate references later.

feedback.reason: Released is already the completed state for this payout ID; repeating the command cannot create another financial effect.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Released is terminal for this ordinary command; replay cannot create another ledger effect.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is settled order and payout ID already released once; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Reopening a completed payout is not an authorized correction path. A second ledger release violates the one-release invariant even if reconciliation is planned.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A correction requires a separate audited process rather than replaying the release transition.
details.transfer: Terminal business transitions should remain stable under repeated commands unless an explicit correction transition exists.

messages.text: Reopening a completed payout is not an authorized correction path.
A second ledger release violates the one-release invariant even if reconciliation is planned.

question.prompt: Transit changes are scheduled with an effective time and sequence. Once a 10:20 platform change becomes effective, a later correction may supersede it but cannot be inserted as an earlier event in the history. Which transition preserves the invariant?

options.text: Rewrite the old notice’s timestamp to 10:19 and reorder the history to make the correction look first.
Delete the old notice and publish the correction as if it were the original change.
Append a correction linked to the notice; preserve actual event order.

feedback.reason: A superseding event records correction without falsifying event order or deleting the original effective change.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A correction is a later linked event; altering or deleting the prior notice falsifies the history.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is effective notice retained; correction records actual ordering; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Changing the old timestamp misrepresents when the first platform instruction took effect. Deleting the old notice erases the history passengers and operators need to explain the change.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A correction can become current without pretending that the earlier transition never occurred.
details.transfer: Preserve the event sequence and represent corrections as new state changes linked to the event they supersede.

messages.text: Changing the old timestamp misrepresents when the first platform instruction took effect.
Deleting the old notice erases the history passengers and operators need to explain the change.

question.prompt: A meter has one committed reservation from 14:00 to 14:30. A new request from 14:20 to 14:40 arrives while the current reservation is still active. No overlaps are allowed. What transition is legal?

options.text: Reject or hold the conflicting request without committing overlap.
Commit both reservations because each request has a valid start and end time.
Move the existing reservation to 14:00–14:20 so both requests fit, without asking its operator.

feedback.reason: The requested intervals overlap for ten minutes, so both cannot be committed under the exclusive-meter invariant.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The intervals overlap, so both cannot be committed and an accepted reservation cannot be silently changed.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is 14:20–14:30 overlap with committed window; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Individually valid endpoints do not make overlapping reservations compatible. Silently changing the existing operator’s reservation violates its accepted interval.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A revised interval can be offered for explicit operator review before it becomes a reservation.
details.transfer: Check the full interval relation at commit time; do not resolve a conflict by silently altering another accepted state.

messages.text: Individually valid endpoints do not make overlapping reservations compatible.
Silently changing the existing operator’s reservation violates its accepted interval.

question.prompt: A caption studio changes providers. The current provider remains active until the replacement passes startup checks; cutover occurs only at a chunk boundary, and clients must not receive a mixed chunk. Startup succeeds but the current chunk has not ended. Which transition is valid now?

options.text: Switch immediately mid-chunk because startup succeeded.
Keep the current provider until the chunk boundary, then cut over.
Report the new provider active while continuing to send the rest of the current chunk from the old provider.

feedback.reason: Readiness satisfies one precondition, but the explicit chunk-boundary rule still blocks cutover at this moment.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Provider readiness and chunk-boundary completion are separate prerequisites; cutover before both risks mixed output.
details.scenarioApplication: The decisive case fact is replacement ready but current chunk not complete; no mixed chunk; the requested state change is checked against it before the new state is recorded.
details.errorCorrection: Immediate switching can split a chunk across providers. The reported provider and actual chunk source would disagree, and clients could see mixed output.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the boundary never arrives, the current provider remains active and the switch remains pending.
details.transfer: Model readiness and safe cutover as separate transition conditions; commit only when both hold.

messages.text: Immediate switching can split a chunk across providers.
The reported provider and actual chunk source would disagree, and clients could see mixed output.
